title: Do This, Then That
overview: Read and listen to short instructions, and give them. Put steps in order with first, next, after that and finally. Give the way to a place: turn left, go straight on. Say where things are: above, below, inside, outside, opposite and under.
learningPath: Words: listen, look and say. 24 words.
Patterns: 4 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: a message, a recipe and a sign.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen.
Writing: a note, steps and the way to a place.
Practice: write. Check with the answers.
Quiz: 12 questions. At the end, My progress.
lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 15.
In this unit, you read, listen to and give instructions.
Instructions tell you what to do.
You see them in a recipe: the steps to make food.
You listen to them in the street: the way to a place.
Listen.
Turn left.
Mix the milk and the sugar.
An instruction starts with the doing word.
Turn. Mix. Stir. Cross.
There is no you at the start.
Not: You turn left. Just: Turn left.
The doing word stays the same. Not turns. Not turning.
Add please to be polite: Please close the door.
Now the steps.
Many instructions have steps: step 1, step 2, step 3.
These words say the order: first, next, then, after that, finally.
Listen to the steps for a cup of tea.
First, boil the water.
Next, put the tea in a cup.
Then, pour the water into the cup.
After that, add some milk.
Finally, stir the tea.
First starts. Finally ends.
Next, then and after that are for the steps in the middle.
Next is not next to. Next to is a place: the bag is next to the bed.
Now directions: the way to a place.
Go straight on. That means the same way, with no turns.
Turn left. Turn right.
Put your hands up in front of you. Your left hand makes an L.
Cross the road at the traffic lights. Wait for the green light.
Listen to two lines. They are not the same.
Turn left: you go that way.
The bank is on the left: the bank is there.
Now six words for where things are.
The clock is above the door.
The bin is below the window.
The bag is under the table.
The milk is inside the fridge.
The bike is outside the shop.
The bank is opposite the park. The road is between them.
After these six words, there is no of.
Not: opposite of the park. Just: opposite the park.
These keep of: at the top of the page, in the middle of the room, at the end of the road.
Now listen to the way to a library.
First, leave the station and turn right.
Next, go straight on to the traffic lights.
After that, cross the road.
Finally, look on your left. The library is opposite the park.
In a recipe, some steps are hot, and some use a knife.
Do those steps with someone to help.
Now you. Say three steps for a cup of tea.
Then say the way from your door to a shop. It can be made up.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

outcomes.outcome: Give short spoken instructions for the kitchen and for the road, with the doing word first and no you.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 1 practice self-checked; Practice 1, eight items; Speaking 1 and 4 recordings; Quiz items 1 and 2.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can give short instructions: Turn left. Stir the tea.

outcomes.outcome: Write the steps of a simple recipe in order with first, next, then, after that and finally.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 2 practice; Practice 2; Writing 2 checklist; Quiz items 3 and 4.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write steps in order: First, … Next, … Finally, …

outcomes.outcome: Understand spoken directions with turn left, turn right, go straight on and cross, and say where they end.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 3 practice; Speaking 2 and 3 recordings checked against the key; Quiz items 6 to 8.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can understand directions: Turn right. Go straight on.

outcomes.outcome: Say and write where a thing or a place is with above, below, inside, outside, opposite and under, and with top, bottom, side, middle and end.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 4 practice; Practice 4 and 6; Speaking 5 recording; Writing 4 checklist; Quiz items 9, 10 and 12.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can say where a thing is: The bank is opposite the park.

outcomes.outcome: Read a short message, a recipe and a sign, and find the step you need.
outcomes.evidence: Reading 1 to 3 questions; Practice 3 and 5; Quiz items 5 and 11.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can read a recipe or a sign and do the steps.

outcomes.outcome: Ask the way politely, and check the directions by saying them back.
outcomes.evidence: Speaking 6 recording and its checklist; the assignment recording.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can ask the way and say the directions back.

outcomes.outcome: Write short instructions: a note for a kitchen, and the way from a bus stop to a place.
outcomes.evidence: Writing 1 and Writing 3 against their checklists; the assignment card.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write short instructions and the way to a place.

words.meaning: One side of you. Put your hands up: the left hand makes an L.
words.example: Turn left at the bank.
practice: The café is on the left.
Turn left, then go straight on.
Look left and right. Then cross the road.
I write with my left hand.
Left is also the past of leave: I left my bag.
words.starter: At the traffic lights, turn left and …
words.tutor: Say two lines to the tutor: Turn left at the … and The … is on the left. Ask it which line is an instruction.

words.meaning: The side of you that is not left.
words.example: Turn right at the traffic lights.
practice: The bank is on the right.
Go straight on, then turn right.
The park is on your right side.
Right can also mean not wrong: That is right.
words.starter: Turn right and the … is on the …
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for five short directions with left or right. Point that way with your hand for each one.

words.meaning: The same way, with no turns.
words.example: Go straight on to the end of the road.
practice: Go straight on. The school is on the left.
Walk straight on to the traffic lights.
No turns here: go straight on.
Is the station straight on? Yes, it is.
words.tutor: Say Go straight on five times to the tutor. Ask it if you said straight as one part, with no extra sound at the start.

words.meaning: Go a new way: to the left or to the right.
words.example: Turn left at the café.
practice: Turn right at the end of the road.
Turn left, then cross the bridge.
The bus turns right at the school.
Please turn the page.
words.tutor: Give the tutor the way from a bus stop to a shop, real or made up. Use turn two times.

words.meaning: Walk or drive from this side of a road to that side.
words.example: Cross the road at the traffic lights.
practice: Look left and right. Then cross.
Cross the bridge and turn left.
We cross the road to the park.
Wait for the green light, then cross.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor three steps to cross a road at traffic lights. Ask it to check that each step starts with the doing word.

words.meaning: Cars and buses go on it. A street is a road in a town.
words.example: The school is at the end of this road.
practice: This road is busy in the morning.
Cross the road here.
The bank is on Station Road.
Walk on the side of the road, not in the middle.
words.tutor: Name three places on a road you know, real or made up. Tell the tutor where each one is: on the left, on the right or at the end.

words.meaning: Three lights at a road: red means stop, and green means go.
words.example: Turn left at the traffic lights.
practice: The traffic lights are red. Stop.
Cross the road at the traffic lights.
Wait: the traffic lights are not green.
Go straight on to the traffic lights.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor what red, yellow and green mean at traffic lights. Say each answer back as a short line.

words.meaning: You walk or drive on it, above water or above a road.
words.example: Cross the bridge to the park.
practice: The bridge is long and white.
A train goes under the bridge.
The café is opposite the bridge.
The station is at the end of the bridge.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor one line with bridge and under, and one line with bridge and cross.

words.meaning: Make two or more things into one, with a spoon.
words.example: Mix the milk and the sugar.
practice: Mix the rice and the water in a bowl.
Mix it with a spoon for a minute.
First, mix the eggs in a bowl.
Red and yellow mix to make orange.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for one simple thing you can make in a bowl. Tell it one step with mix.

words.meaning: Make two from one, with a knife or scissors.
words.example: Cut the apple with a knife.
practice: Cut the paper with scissors.
Cut the bread, with someone to help.
Cut the banana and put it in the bowl.
Please cut the card in the middle.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor two things you cut with scissors and one thing you cut with a knife.

words.meaning: Put one more thing in.
words.example: Add some milk to the tea.
practice: Add salt to the rice.
Next, add two eggs.
Add your name at the bottom.
Add sugar, then stir it.
words.tutor: Say the steps for a cup of tea to the tutor, four steps. Put add in one of them.

words.meaning: Make water or milk go out of a bottle or a cup.
words.example: Pour the milk into a glass.
practice: Pour the water slowly.
Pour the tea into two cups.
Then, pour the milk on the rice.
Pour sounds like door and floor.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor what you pour into a cup in the morning. Say it as an instruction: Pour the … .

words.meaning: Make water very, very hot. It moves and makes a sound.
words.example: Boil the water for the tea.
practice: Boil the eggs for ten minutes.
The water is boiling. It is very hot.
Boil the rice, with someone to help.
First, boil some water in the kitchen.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor how many minutes to boil an egg. Say its answer back as an instruction: Boil the egg for … minutes.

words.meaning: Make a thing hot.
words.example: Heat the milk for two minutes.
practice: Heat the rice again for lunch.
Heat the water. It is hot, not boiling.
Heat it, with someone to help.
Heat and hot: heat makes a thing hot.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor one line with heat and one line with boil. Ask it: which one makes water move and make a sound?

words.meaning: Turn a spoon in a cup or a bowl, again and again.
words.example: Stir the tea with a spoon.
practice: Finally, stir the tea.
Stir it for one minute.
Add sugar and stir.
Stir the rice. It is very hot.
words.tutor: Say three steps for a cup of tea to the tutor. Make the last one: Finally, stir the tea.

words.meaning: After this one. Next comes after first.
words.example: First, boil the water. Next, add the tea.
practice: Next, turn left at the bank.
What is the next step?
Next, pour the milk.
Next is not next to. Next to is a place.
words.tutor: Say two steps to the tutor, with first and next. Ask it for the step after that, and say all three.

words.meaning: Last of all. It starts the last step.
words.example: Finally, stir the tea.
practice: Finally, cross the bridge.
Finally, write your name at the bottom.
Finally, the café is on the right.
Finally has two l: fin-al-ly.
words.tutor: Give the tutor four steps with first, next, after that and finally. Ask it if finally is on the last step.

words.meaning: One thing to do, in a list of things to do.
words.example: Step 1: wash the rice.
practice: This recipe has six steps.
Read each step, then do it.
The last step is easy.
One step, two steps.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor a thing you can make or do in three steps. Say Step 1, Step 2 and Step 3.

words.meaning: Words that tell you what to do, step by step.
words.example: Read the instructions first.
practice: The instructions are on the box.
Read the instructions, one step at a time.
Can you give me instructions to the station?
One instruction, two instructions.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for short instructions to clean a table. Say each step back to it.

words.meaning: The part of a thing that is up. A page starts at the top.
words.example: Write your name at the top of the page.
practice: The cups are on the top shelf.
The top of the box is red.
The clock is at the top of the building.
Top and bottom: up and down.
words.starter: At the top of the page, …
words.tutor: Look at a page or a screen. Tell the tutor what is at the top of it.

words.meaning: The part of a thing that is down, not the top. A page ends at the bottom.
words.example: My keys are at the bottom of my bag.
practice: Write the date at the bottom of the page.
The big books are on the bottom shelf.
Finally, write your name at the bottom.
The bottom of the cup is wet.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor two things at the bottom of a bag or a box, real or made up.

words.meaning: The left or the right part of a thing or a place.
words.example: The bank is on this side of the road.
practice: The door is on the left side.
A box has four sides, a top and a bottom.
Walk on the side of the road.
Cross to that side of the road.
words.starter: The … is on the left side of the …
words.tutor: Tell the tutor where two things are in a room: one on the left side and one on the right side.

words.meaning: The part between the two ends, or between the two sides.
words.example: The table is in the middle of the room.
practice: Stop in the middle of the bridge.
The bank is in the middle of the street.
Cut the card in the middle.
Three cups: the middle one is blue.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a table: what is in the middle of it, and what is at the sides?

words.meaning: The last part of a thing: a road, a film or a day.
words.example: The café is at the end of the street.
practice: Go straight on to the end of the road.
At the end of the film, the family is happy.
A full stop goes at the end.
The end of the week is the weekend.
words.starter: At the end of the road, …
words.tutor: Give the tutor directions that finish with: It is at the end of the road. Ask it to say the way back to you.

grammar.title: Instructions: Turn left. Stir the tea.
grammar.explanation:
An instruction tells someone what to do.
It starts with the doing word: Turn. Stir. Cross.
There is no you at the start.
It is the same for one person or for ten.
grammar.rule:
Turn left.
Go straight on.
Cross the road.
Mix the milk and the sugar.
Pour the water into a cup.
Stir the tea.

To be polite, add please:
Please close the door.
Close the door, please.

The doing word stays the same:
Turn. Not: turns, turning.

One instruction on each line.
A full stop at the end.
grammar.workedExample:
Make an instruction: you / the window / open.
1. Find the doing word: open.
2. Put it first: Open.
3. Then the thing: Open the window.
4. Leave out you.
5. Add please: Please open the window.
6. Check: the doing word first, a full stop last. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to start with you, or to add -s or -ing.
No: You turn left.
No: Turns left.
No: Turning left.
Yes: Turn left.
grammar.tip: Doing word first, full stop last.
grammar.practice:
Make an instruction. Put the words in order.
1. left / turn
2. the road / cross
3. the tea / stir
4. the window / open / please
5. the water / boil
6. on / straight / go
7. the milk / add
8. your name / write / please
grammar.answers:
1. Turn left.  2. Cross the road.  3. Stir the tea.  4. Please open the window. Or: Open the window, please.  5. Boil the water.  6. Go straight on.  7. Add the milk.  8. Please write your name. Or: Write your name, please.
Wrong on 6? Go is the doing word, so it comes first. Straight on stays together.
Did you start with you? Leave it out. The doing word comes first.

grammar.title: Steps in order: next, after that, finally
grammar.explanation:
Many instructions have steps.
These words say the order: first, next, then, after that, finally.
Put the word at the start of the step.
After it, write a comma.
grammar.rule:
First, boil the water.
Next, put the tea in a cup.
Then, pour the water into the cup.
After that, add some milk.
Finally, stir the tea.

first: step 1
next, then, after that: the steps in the middle
finally: the last step

The middle words can go in any order.
Finally is for the last step only.

Next is not next to.
Next, turn left. That is a step.
The bag is next to the bed. That is a place.
grammar.workedExample:
Put the steps in order: a cup of tea.
Add some milk. / Stir it. / Boil the water. / Pour the water into a cup.
1. What comes first? Hot water. First, boil the water.
2. The water goes in the cup. Next, pour the water into a cup.
3. Then the milk. After that, add some milk.
4. The last step: Finally, stir it.
5. Check: first on step 1, finally on the last step. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to use finally too early.
No: First, boil the water. Finally, add the milk. Next, stir it.
Yes: First, boil the water. Next, add the milk. Finally, stir it.
Finally always starts the last step.
grammar.practice:
Write first, next, after that or finally. Use each word one time in 1 to 4, and again in 5 to 8.
Make rice:
1. ___, wash the rice in cold water.
2. ___, put the rice in the water.
3. ___, boil the rice for twenty minutes.
4. ___, add some salt and eat it.
Cross a road:
5. ___, walk to the traffic lights.
6. ___, wait for the green light.
7. ___, look left and right.
8. ___, cross the road.
grammar.answers:
1. First  2. Next  3. After that  4. Finally  5. First  6. Next  7. After that  8. Finally
Then is right in 2, 3, 6 and 7 too.
2 After that and 3 Next is right too. So is 6 After that and 7 Next.
Wrong on 4 or 8? Finally is only for the last step.

grammar.title: Which way: left, right and straight on
grammar.explanation:
Directions tell someone the way to a place.
Use go, turn and cross.
Straight on means the same way, with no turns.
On the left and on the right say where the place is.
grammar.rule:
Go straight on.
Turn left.
Turn right.
Turn left at the bank.
Turn right at the traffic lights.
Cross the road.
Cross the bridge.
Go to the end of the road.

Where the place is:
The bank is on the left.
The park is on the right.

Turn left: you go that way.
On the left: the place is there.
grammar.workedExample:
You are at the station. You want the café.
Walk to the traffic lights. Go left there.
The café is on your left.
1. To the traffic lights, with no turns: Go straight on.
2. At the traffic lights, go left: Turn left at the traffic lights.
3. Where is the café? The café is on the left.
4. Say it all: Go straight on. Turn left at the traffic lights. The café is on the left.
5. Check: turn left for the move, on the left for the place. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to mix up turn left and on the left.
No: Turn on the left at the bank.
Yes: Turn left at the bank.
No: The bank is left.
Yes: The bank is on the left.
grammar.tip: Turn left: you move. On the left: it is there.
grammar.practice:
Write the right words.
1. (Turn left / Turn on the left) at the bank.
2. The school is (left / on the left).
3. Go (straight on / straight on the left) to the bridge.
4. (Cross / Turn) the road at the traffic lights.
5. The park is (on the right / at right).
6. (Turn right / Right turn) at the end of the road.
7. (Go / Goes) straight on.
8. (Cross / Crossing) the bridge to the station.
grammar.answers:
1. Turn left  2. on the left  3. straight on  4. Cross  5. on the right  6. Turn right  7. Go  8. Cross
Wrong on 1 or 2? Turn left is the move. On the left is the place.
Wrong on 7 or 8? An instruction starts with the doing word as it is: Go, Cross.

grammar.title: Above, below, inside, outside, opposite, under
grammar.explanation:
These six words say where a thing is.
The word comes first, then the place: above the door, inside the fridge.
After these six words, there is no of.
grammar.rule:
The clock is above the door.
The bin is below the window.
The bag is under the table.
The milk is inside the fridge.
The bike is outside the shop.
The bank is opposite the park.

above: up from it
below: down from it
under: down from it, with the thing on top
inside: in it
outside: not in it
opposite: the road or the room is between them

These keep of:
at the top of the page
at the bottom of the bag
in the middle of the room
at the end of the road
on the left side of the street
grammar.workedExample:
Where is the key? It is in a box. The box is on the floor. The bed is on top of it.
1. The key and the box: in it. Say inside.
2. The key is inside the box.
3. The box and the bed: the bed is on top. Say under.
4. The box is under the bed.
5. Check: no of after inside or under. Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to add of after these words.
No: The bank is opposite of the park.
Yes: The bank is opposite the park.
No: The key is inside of the box.
Yes: The key is inside the box.
grammar.tip: Opposite the park, inside the box: no of.
grammar.practice:
Write above, below, inside, outside, opposite or under.
1. The fish is ___ the fridge. It is cold in there.
2. The clock is on the wall, ___ the door. You look up at it.
3. The bikes are ___ the shop, on the street.
4. The box is ___ the table. The table is on top of it.
5. The café is ___ the bank. The road is between them.
6. The question is at the top of the page. Your answer goes down from it. Write it ___ the question.
7. Wait ___ the door, in the street. Come in when I call you.
grammar.answers:
1. inside  2. above  3. outside  4. under  5. opposite  6. below (under is OK too)  7. outside
Wrong on 4? With a thing on top, say under.
Wrong on 5? Opposite: the road is between the two places.
Did you write of after the word? Leave it out: opposite the bank.

readings.title: A Message: The Way to the Café
readings.setting: Dan sends a message to Eva. She is at the bus station.
readings.passage:
Hi Eva! Here is the way to the café.
First, leave the bus station and turn right.
Next, go straight on to the traffic lights.
Cross the road at the lights. Wait for the green light!
After that, turn left into Bank Street.
Go straight on to the end of the street.
There is a small bridge. Cross it.
Finally, look on your left.
The café is opposite the park, next to the chemist.
It has a big red door and tables outside.
I am at a table inside, near the window.
See you soon!
Dan

readings.title: Rice with Milk and Banana
readings.setting: A recipe card on a kitchen wall.
readings.passage:
RICE WITH MILK AND BANANA
For two people. Time: 40 minutes.
You need:
1 cup of rice
3 cups of water
2 cups of milk
2 spoons of sugar
1 banana
Do the hot steps and the cutting with someone to help.
Step 1: Wash the rice in cold water.
Step 2: Boil the water. Add the rice.
Step 3: Heat it for twenty minutes. Stir it sometimes.
Step 4: Pour in the milk and add the sugar.
Step 5: Stir it for ten minutes more.
Step 6: Cut the banana and put it on top.
Finally, wait five minutes. It is very hot!

readings.title: Bridge Closed
readings.setting: A sign at the start of a bridge in a town.
readings.passage:
BRIDGE CLOSED
From Monday the 3rd to Friday the 14th
The bridge is closed for work.
Walking to the station?
Turn right here and go straight on to the traffic lights.
Cross the road at the lights.
The station is on the left, opposite the bank.
Walking to the market?
Turn left here. The market is at the end of this road.
Cars and bikes: turn left at the end of this road.
Buses: the number 7 bus stops outside the library.
Thank you.

comprehension.why: Line 2: First, leave the bus station and turn right.

comprehension.q: What does Eva do at the traffic lights?
comprehension.a: She waits for the green light. Then she crosses the road.
comprehension.why: Line 4: Cross the road at the lights. Wait for the green light!

comprehension.q: Eva is at the end of Bank Street. What is her next step?
comprehension.why: Lines 6 and 7: Go straight on to the end of the street. There is a small bridge. Cross it.

comprehension.q: Line 8 starts with Finally. What does that tell Eva?
comprehension.a: It is the last step. The café is near now.
comprehension.why: Finally starts the last step. After line 8, the message says where the café is.

comprehension.q: Eva is at the end of the way. The park is on her right. Where is the café?
comprehension.a: On her left, opposite the park.
comprehension.why: Line 8: look on your left. Line 9: The café is opposite the park.

comprehension.a: Wash the rice in cold water.
comprehension.why: Step 1: Wash the rice in cold water.

comprehension.q: Step 3 says: Stir it sometimes. What do you do?
comprehension.a: Turn a spoon in the rice, again and again, some of the time.
comprehension.why: Stir: turn a spoon, again and again. Sometimes: not all the time.

comprehension.q: Which steps need someone to help you, and why?
comprehension.a: Steps 2 to 5: they are hot. Step 6: you cut with a knife.
comprehension.why: The card says: Do the hot steps and the cutting with someone to help. Steps 2 to 5 boil, heat and stir. Step 6 is cut.

comprehension.q: You are walking to the station. What do you do first?
comprehension.a: Turn right here and go straight on to the traffic lights.
comprehension.why: The sign says: Walking to the station? Turn right here and go straight on to the traffic lights.

comprehension.q: It is Wednesday the 9th. Can you walk on the bridge?
comprehension.a: No. It is closed from the 3rd to the 14th.
comprehension.why: Line 2: From Monday the 3rd to Friday the 14th. The 9th is between them.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Say the instruction
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each instruction.
Turn left.
Go straight on.
Cross the road.
Boil the water.
Pour the milk into a cup.
Stir the tea, please.
Tap the mic. Say the 6 instructions.
Tap the mic again. Listen.
Check: does each one start with the doing word? Is there no you at the start?
speaking.tutor: Say six instructions to the tutor: three for the road and three for the kitchen. Ask it to tell you any that start with you or end in -s.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Straight, traffic, cross, bridge
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat. These words start with two sounds together.
step, stir, straight
traffic, train
cross
bridge, bread
Say each one slowly. Then say it quickly.
Now three lines.
Go straight on.
Stop at the traffic lights.
Cross the bridge.
Tap the mic. Say the 3 lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: two sounds together, with no extra sound between them? Straight is one part, not two.
speaking.tutor: Say straight, traffic, cross and bridge to the tutor. Ask it which word had an extra sound at the start, if any.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Where are you now?
speaking.instructions:
Listen. You are at the bus station.
Here is the map, in words.
Station Road goes from the bus station to the traffic lights.
At the traffic lights, the bank is to the left.
The post office is to the right.
After the traffic lights, go straight on. The library is at the end of the road.
Now listen. Where are you at the end of each one?
1. Go straight on to the traffic lights. Turn left.
2. Go straight on to the traffic lights. Turn right.
3. Go straight on. Cross at the traffic lights. Go to the end of the road.
Say each answer: I am at the ___.
Tap the mic. Say 3 answers. Tap again. Listen.
Check with the key: 1 the bank. 2 the post office. 3 the library.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Listen. You are at the bus station.
Here is the map, in words.
Station Road goes from the bus station to the traffic lights.
At the traffic lights, the bank is to the left.
The post office is to the right.
After the traffic lights, go straight on. The library is at the end of the road.
Now listen. Where are you at the end of each one?
1. Go straight on to the traffic lights. Turn left.
2. Go straight on to the traffic lights. Turn right.
3. Go straight on. Cross at the traffic lights. Go to the end of the road.
Say each answer: I am at the …
Tap the mic. Say 3 answers. Tap again. Listen.
Check with the key: 1 the bank. 2 the post office. 3 the library.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for directions in a made-up town, three steps long. Say where you are at the end, then ask it if you are right.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — How to make a cup of tea
speaking.instructions:
Say how to make a cup of tea in five steps.
Use first, next, then, after that and finally.
Here are the steps. They are not in order.
stir the tea
boil the water
add some milk
put the tea in a cup
pour the water into the cup
Say them in order. Start each one with a step word.
Tap the mic. Say the 5 steps. Tap again. Listen.
Check: first on step 1? Finally on step 5? A doing word after each step word?
Now say the steps for a thing you can make. It can be simple, like a cup of coffee.
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor the steps for a simple thing you can make, with first, next, after that and finally. Ask it if a step is missing.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Where is it in the room?
speaking.instructions:
Look at a room: at home, at school or at work.
Say where 5 things are.
Use above, below, inside, outside, opposite or under.
Listen to the model first.
The clock is above the door.
My bag is under the table.
The pens are inside my bag.
The bin is below the window.
The window is opposite the door.
Tap the mic. Say 5 lines about your room. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 5 lines? A new place word in each line? No of after the place word?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor where five things are in a room, real or made up. Then ask it to say where one new thing is. Draw it on paper to check you understand.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Asking the way
speaking.instructions:
You are in a town. You want the post office.
Listen. Say your lines.
You: Hello. Can you help me? Where is the post office, please?
Person: Go straight on to the bridge. Cross the bridge. Then turn right.
You: Cross the bridge, then turn right?
Person: Yes. The post office is on the left, opposite the café.
You: Opposite the café. Thank you!
Person: OK. Goodbye!
Say the steps back. That is how you check you understand.
Tap the mic. Say your 3 lines. Tap again. Listen.
Now ask the way to the library or the bank. Change the words.
Check: please in your question? Did you say the steps back?
A friend can read the person's lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor the way to a place in a made-up town. Say its directions back to it, step by step, and ask if you have them right.

writing.title: Writing 1 — A note for a kitchen
writing.prompt:
Write 5 instructions for a kitchen at home, at school or at work.
They go on a note on the wall.
Start each one with a doing word or with Please.
writing.model:
KITCHEN NOTE
Please wash your cup.
Put the milk inside the fridge.
Close the fridge door.
Clean the table, please.
Put the spoons on the shelf.
writing.criteria:
5 instructions.
Each one starts with a doing word or with Please.
No you at the start.
A capital letter and a full stop in each line.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change one word in each line: cup, milk, door, table, spoons.
Then say each line out loud.
writing.extension: Add a line with a place word: Put the cups above the fridge.

writing.title: Writing 2 — Steps for a simple drink
writing.prompt:
Write 5 steps for a simple drink or food.
Use first, next, then, after that and finally.
On a hot or a cutting step, write: with someone to help.
writing.model:
MILK WITH BANANA
First, cut a banana, with someone to help.
Next, put the banana in a bowl.
Then, add a glass of milk.
After that, mix it with a spoon.
Finally, pour it into a glass.
writing.criteria:
5 steps, in order.
First on step 1 and finally on step 5.
A comma after each step word.
A doing word after each comma.
writing.support:
Write the 5 doing words first, in order: cut, put, add, mix, pour.
Then put a step word in front of each one.
writing.extension: Add a line at the top: You need. Write 3 things under it, like Reading 2.

writing.title: Writing 3 — The way to a place
writing.prompt:
Write the way from a bus stop to a place.
The place can be a shop, a library or a café.
It can be a real town or a made-up town.
Use turn, go straight on and cross, and the step words.
writing.model:
The way to the library
First, leave the bus stop and turn left.
Next, go straight on to the traffic lights.
After that, cross the road.
Finally, turn right. The library is on the left, opposite the bank.
writing.starter: First, leave the bus stop and turn
writing.criteria:
4 or 5 steps.
A step word at the start of each step.
Turn left or turn right in one step or more.
One line with on the left or on the right for the place.
writing.support:
Draw the way on paper first: one line for each road.
Write one step for each line on your drawing.
Then add the step words.
writing.extension: Add one more line: what the place looks like. It has a big red door.

writing.title: Writing 4 — Where to find things
writing.prompt:
A friend or someone in your family needs three things.
They are in your room or on your desk.
Write a note: where are they?
Use above, below, inside, outside, opposite or under.
The person and the things can be made up.
writing.model:
Hi Sam,
My keys are inside the blue bag, under the desk.
The book is on the shelf above the bed.
My phone is on the table, opposite the window.
Thanks!
writing.criteria:
3 things, and where each one is.
3 place words from this unit, one for each thing.
No of after above, below, inside, outside, opposite or under.
A capital letter and a full stop in each sentence.
writing.support:
Write three short lines first: key, bag, inside.
Then make each one a sentence: The key is inside the bag.
writing.extension:
Add a line with top, bottom or end.
Like this: The pen is at the bottom of the bag.

activities.title: Practice 1 — The doing word
activities.instructions:
Write the doing word. Use each word one time.
boil, cross, cut, pour, stir, turn, add, mix
1. ___ the road at the traffic lights.
2. ___ the water. It is very hot, and it moves.
3. ___ the milk into a glass.
4. ___ left at the bank.
5. ___ the apple with a knife, with someone to help.
6. ___ the tea with a spoon, again and again.
7. ___ some salt to the rice.
8. ___ the eggs and the milk in a bowl.
activities.answers:
1. Cross  2. Boil  3. Pour  4. Turn  5. Cut  6. Stir  7. Add  8. Mix
Wrong on 6 or 8? Stir: turn a spoon in one thing. Mix: make two things into one.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 1 and the Cooking words, and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud with your word. Write the word. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Put the steps in order
activities.instructions:
Put the steps in order. Write the numbers.
A. A cup of tea:
1. Stir it.
2. Boil the water.
3. Put the tea in a cup.
4. Add some milk.
5. Pour the water into the cup.
B. Cross a road:
6. Cross the road.
7. Walk to the traffic lights.
8. Look left and right.
9. Wait for the green light.
C. Now write set A with first, next, then, after that and finally.
activities.answers:
A. 2, 3, 5, 4, 1. (3, 2, 5, 4, 1 is right too.)
B. 7, 9, 8, 6. (7, 8, 9, 6 is right too.)
C. First, boil the water. Next, put the tea in a cup. Then, pour the water into the cup. After that, add some milk. Finally, stir it.
Wrong in A? First the water goes in the cup. Then the milk. You stir last.
A and B right: good.
One wrong: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write the steps on small cards, one on each. Move the cards into order. Then check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Read the directions
activities.instructions:
Read the directions. Then answer.
From the station: Turn left. Go straight on to the traffic lights. Turn right. Cross the bridge. The market is at the end of the road, on the left.
1. What is the first instruction?
2. Where do you turn right?
3. What do you cross?
4. Is the market at the start or at the end of the road?
5. Is the market on the left or on the right?
6. How many instructions start with a doing word?
activities.answers:
1. Turn left.  2. At the traffic lights.  3. The bridge.  4. At the end.  5. On the left.  6. Four: turn, go, turn and cross.
Wrong on 6? The last line says where the market is. It is not an instruction.
5 or 6 right: good.
4 or less: read the directions again, one line at a time.
activities.solo: Point at each line as you read it. Write your answers. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Where is it?
activities.instructions:
Write above, below, inside, outside, opposite or under.
1. The cups are in the box. They are ___ the box.
2. The clock is on the wall, up from the window. It is ___ the window.
3. The bike is on the street, not in the shop. It is ___ the shop.
4. The bag is on the floor. The chair is on top of it. The bag is ___ the chair.
5. The road is between the café and the bank. The café is ___ the bank.
6. The bin is on the floor, down from the window. It is ___ the window.
7. It is cold on the street. Wait ___ the café.
8. You are in the café. The bus stop is on the street. It is ___ the café.
activities.answers:
1. inside  2. above  3. outside  4. under  5. opposite  6. below (under is OK too)  7. inside  8. outside
Wrong on 5? Opposite: a road or a room is between the two things.
Did you write of after the word? Leave it out.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 4 and do it again.
activities.solo: Draw a small picture for each line. Write the word. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Match the word
activities.instructions:
Match 1 to 8 with a to h.
1. bridge
2. traffic lights
3. boil
4. pour
5. step
6. instructions
7. middle
8. cross
a. Make water very, very hot.
b. Red means stop, and green means go.
c. You walk or drive on it, above water.
d. One thing to do in a list of things to do.
e. Words that tell you what to do.
f. Go from this side of a road to that side.
g. Make milk go out of a bottle into a glass.
h. The part between the two ends.
activities.answers:
1c  2b  3a  4g  5d  6e  7h  8f
Check 5 and 6: a step is one thing to do. Instructions are all the steps.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: go back to Words, listen again, and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each word out loud. Write the letter. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Top, bottom, side, middle, end
activities.instructions:
Write top, bottom, side, middle or end.
1. Write your name at the ___ of the page. It is the first line.
2. The café is at the ___ of the road. After it, there is no more road.
3. The keys are at the ___ of my bag, under the books.
4. The table is in the ___ of the room.
5. The bank is on the left ___ of the street.
6. A full stop goes at the ___ of a sentence.
7. The big clock is at the ___ of the building. Look up!
activities.answers:
1. top  2. end  3. bottom  4. middle  5. side  6. end  7. top
Wrong on 3? Under the books means down in the bag: the bottom.
6 or 7 right: good.
5 or less: read the Parts of a place words and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud. Write the word. Check with the key.

options: You turns left at the bank.
The bank is on the left.
quizzes.why: An instruction starts with the doing word: Turn left. You turns has you and an -s. The bank is on the left says where the bank is. Turning has -ing.
An instruction starts with the doing word as it is: Boil the water. Boils has an -s. Boiling has -ing. An instruction has no you at the start.

quizzes.q: First, boil the water. ___, pour it into a cup. Finally, add milk.
quizzes.why: Next is for a step in the middle. Finally is on the last step here, and first is on step 1. Next to is a place, not a step.

quizzes.q: Which word starts the last step?
quizzes.why: Finally means last of all. First starts step 1. Next and then are for the steps in the middle.

quizzes.q: Step 1: Wash the rice. Step 2: Boil the water. Step 3: Add the rice. What is the second step?
quizzes.why: The second step is Step 2: Boil the water. Wash the rice is step 1, and add the rice is step 3. Eat the rice is not on the card.

quizzes.q: You are at the traffic lights. The park is to the right. What is the instruction?
quizzes.why: The park is to the right, so turn right. Turn on the right is wrong: say turn right. Turn left goes to the left, not to the park. Right you turn has the words in the wrong order.
Go straight on: the same way, with no turns. Left needs turn: Turn left. Cross and step are doing words, so they do not go after go.

quizzes.q: Which one says where the café is?
options: The café is on the left.
quizzes.a: The café is on the left.
quizzes.why: On the left says where a place is. Turn left at the café is an instruction to move. The café is left needs on the. You cross a road, not a café.

quizzes.q: The milk is in the fridge. The milk is ___ the fridge.
quizzes.why: In the fridge is inside the fridge. Outside is not in it. Opposite has a room or a road between. Above is up from it.

options: The bank is opposite of the park.
The bank is opposite the park.
The bank opposite is the park.
The bank is opposites the park.
quizzes.a: The bank is opposite the park.
quizzes.why: After opposite, there is no of: opposite the park. Opposite of has an extra word. The bank opposite is has the words in the wrong order. Opposite never takes an -s.

quizzes.q: A sign says: BRIDGE CLOSED. Walking to the station? Turn right here. You are walking to the station. What do you do?
quizzes.why: The sign says: Turn right here. The bridge is closed, so you can't cross it. Turn left is the way to the market. Waiting does not take you to the station.

quizzes.q: You write your name on the first line of a page. Where is it?
options: At the bottom of the page.
In the middle of the page.
At the end of the page.
At the top of the page.
quizzes.a: At the top of the page.
quizzes.why: A page starts at the top. The first line is at the top. The bottom and the end are the last line. The middle is between the top and the bottom.

teacherNotes.note: Every card shows one item done before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a short checklist. If you are helping, listen to the recordings together and point at the checklist rather than correcting mid-sentence. Speaking 3 is the listening check: play it once, and let the learner answer before looking at the key.

teacherNotes.type: The two errors worth your attention
teacherNotes.note: First, turn left and on the left get swapped: Turn on the left at the bank, or The bank is left. Pattern 3 sets them side by side; point at the line and ask, is this the move or the place? Second, of after the new place words: opposite of the park, inside of the box. The tip line is the whole rule. Some place words keep of (at the top of, in the middle of, at the end of), and Pattern 4 shows those beside the six that do not.

No task asks the learner to cook or to cross a real road. Every hot or cutting step in the recipes says with someone to help, and Writing 2 asks the learner to write the same words on those steps. The town, its streets and its bridge are made up. For a young learner, the recipe is for reading, not for cooking alone.

Instructions here are positive only: Turn left, Stir the tea. Do not and don't with an instruction are not taught, and the learner is never asked to write one. First is known from Unit 6 and then from Unit 13; here they are used as step words at the start of an instruction, with a comma. Left is also the past of leave from Unit 10 (I left my bag); the Words page says so once, and it is worth saying again if the learner looks puzzled.

The AI tutor is a rehearsal partner, not a marking service, and no task is scored by it alone. Places, people and things in the writing tasks can all be made up. Keep that wording, and never ask the learner to give the tutor a real address or the real way to their home.

selfAssessment.statement: I can give short instructions: Turn left. Stir the tea.
I can write steps in order with first, next and finally.
I can understand directions: turn left, turn right, go straight on.
I can say where a thing is: The bank is opposite the park.
I can read a recipe or a sign and do the steps.
I can ask the way and say the directions back.
I can write the way to a place.

assignment.title: Show the way
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Tap the mic. Give the way from a bus stop to a place.
The place is in a made-up town.
Say 4 steps with first, next, after that and finally.
Then say where the place is.
Like this: The library is on the left, opposite the park.
2. Write a recipe card for a simple drink or food, like Writing 2.
Write 5 steps in order.
On a hot or a cutting step, write: with someone to help.
The town and the recipe can be made up.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written card
